rationale: The simulation layer takes the starting quarterback from the nflverse depth chart, and on the first live Week 2 2026 slate that source was wrong about Minnesota: it ranked Kyler Murray QB1 and Carson Wentz QB2, while Kalshi listed a full starter's passing ladder for Wentz (market-implied mean 215 yards, 1.30 passing touchdowns) and no passing market for Murray at all. The football model therefore gave Wentz 8.5 passing yards and a 0.014 probability of reaching 150, against a market mid of 0.795. The model read its source faithfully; the source was wrong, and a whole team's passing game was attributed to the wrong player. This is the Week 1 Price/Stevenson role-allocation failure moved to the position that determines a team's entire passing volume, and it is the highest-leverage remaining input error in the layer. 26 of the other 27 listed quarterbacks on that slate agreed with the market inside about 15%, so the failure is rare but severe when it fires, and it contaminates more than the quarterback's own line: the team's pass attempts, completion rate and sack rate all carry the wrong player's priors, which moves every receiver on that team.
features: STRICTLY POINT-IN-TIME ROLE AND ELIGIBILITY SIGNALS ONLY: depth-chart rank at the cutoff (daily snapshots from 2025); weekly roster status; injury designation from the content-addressed vintage at the cutoff plus the newest Sleeper capture at or before it; the previous week's actual starter (whoever took the first offensive snap or the plurality of attempts); recent snap and attempt share over a decayed prior window; transaction data (signings, trades, activations, elevations) where a dated free source exists; a named-starter announcement ONLY if a reproducible free source with a per-row publication instant exists -- a file-level date_pulled that moves when the file is rebuilt does not qualify, which is why FTN scheme data was rejected for the rushing work; the EXISTENCE of a substantial passing ladder for a player in the Kalshi universe, and the Kalshi KXSTARTINGQB family IF it turns out to be usable, which the archive says it is not: the only ticker present is KXSTARTINGQBWEEK1, a Week-1-only market with no Week 2 or later equivalent and no 2025 history, so its single week of coverage is also the 2026 development-diagnostic week and cannot serve as validation. Treat that arm as unavailable unless the family reappears with real history. HARD CONSTRAINT: the market may contribute only EXISTENCE and LIQUIDITY, i.e. 'the market believes this player is expected to take the snaps'. No price, midpoint, bid, ask or implied mean may enter the football-only starter determination. The project already accepts existence as a role signal (research/simulation_engine/role_signal_2025.json) and already forbids the quote outside the reconciliation layer; this hypothesis inherits both.
target: PRIMARY: accuracy of the predicted starting quarterback against the realised starter (first offensive snap; plurality of attempts as a tiebreak) on every team-game of a walk-forward evaluation, compared against the depth-chart-only baseline the simulator ships today. SECONDARY: the downstream cost of getting it wrong -- team-level pass attempts, completions and passing-yards MAE, and player-level passing-yards and passing-touchdown MAE and ladder Brier, on the subset of team-games where the baseline and the candidate disagree. TERTIARY: on the 2025 Kalshi archive, the paired Brier of the football-only passing-family probabilities on those disputed team-games, since that is the population the error actually damages.
expected_direction: The depth-chart-only baseline is already right on the large majority of team-games, so the candidate must be judged on the DISAGREEMENT subset, not on overall accuracy where both agree. A candidate earns deployment only if it (a) strictly improves starter accuracy on a walk-forward split, (b) improves team and player passing error on the disagreement subset, and (c) does not degrade any season of the existing 2023-2025 walk-forward. The rushing ablation is the precedent for refusing a signal that passes a direction test but fails materiality: an arm that improves the metric by 0.2% for four parameters was not deployed.
test_plan: PROPOSED, NOT FITTED. Nothing here may be fitted or selected using Week 2 2026, and the Minnesota case may not be used as the selection criterion -- it is the observation that motivated the hypothesis, which makes it the worst possible validation set. Procedure: (1) build the realised-starter label for 2016-2025 from play-by-play (first offensive snap, plurality of attempts as tiebreak); (2) reconstruct each candidate signal as of a point-in-time cutoff for every team-week, using the same vintage discipline as features.fit_priors and prospective.injury_vintage, and record coverage and the first season each signal exists; (3) fit candidates on seasons strictly before an evaluation season and score walk-forward across 2023-2025, exactly as scripts/sim/walkforward.py does, with the depth-chart-only rule as the baseline; (4) report the disagreement-subset table (baseline vs each candidate vs combined) in the ablation format of research/simulation_engine/RUSHING_ABLATION.md, including the arms that were REJECTED and why; (5) only then, if a candidate passes all three conditions, preregister a prospective test as a new hypothesis id before it is deployed. Kalshi listing existence is only available from the 2025 archive onward, so a listing-based arm can be fitted on 2025 and confirmed on held-out 2025 weeks at best, and its thin history must be stated as a limitation rather than averaged away. The KXSTARTINGQB arm is currently unavailable on the evidence (KXSTARTINGQBWEEK1 only, no history), so the practical candidate set is the nflverse/roster/injury/prior-starter/snap-share group plus passing-ladder existence.
dataset: nflverse play-by-play and weekly rosters 2016-2026 for the realised-starter label and the snap/attempt shares; data/raw/nflverse/_vintages for dated depth-chart and injury snapshots; market-data data/context for Sleeper captures; market-data data/kalshi for the 2025 ladder universe (existence only) and any KXSTARTINGQB history; research/simulation_engine for the existing walk-forward baseline.
result: UNTESTED. Nothing has been fitted. The motivating observation is recorded in research/simulation_engine/WEEK2_2026_SLATE_AUDIT.md and detected every cycle by the quarterback cross-check in scripts/sim/slate_audit.py.
notes: CONTAINMENT WHILE THIS IS UNTESTED, verified on the published Week 2 artifact: pass_yards and pass_td both deploy a reconciliation weight of 0, so a misattributed passing line is reported at the market mean and carries no deviation authority; after PR #28 a zero-weight family cannot enter largest_reconciled_disagreements and cannot raise a game's review priority; and the quarterback cross-check in the slate audit fails the cycle whenever the market lists a starter's passing ladder (implied mean >= 80 yards) for a player the football model projects below 35% of it. The failure is therefore visible and inert rather than silent and priced. DELIBERATELY NOT HOTFIXED: selecting Wentz by hand, or wiring a listing-existence rule chosen because it fixes this slate, would be fitting to the evaluation period -- the same error the temporal-leakage round was about. The Minnesota game is a Sunday game; Thursday's two starting quarterbacks were both correct.
